h2: Atlanta NDT training providers compared: ATS courses in Marietta, Chattanooga State, welding schools and self-paced online theory
html:
Atlanta NDT training providers compared: ATS courses in Marietta, Chattanooga State, welding schools and self-paced online theory

Atlanta is better served for in-person NDT instruction than most Southern metros, and the range is wide: short method courses at a commercial testing company, a two-year college programme a couple of hours up I-75, welding schools that touch on inspection, and online theory with the practical done at work. The page above covers where Atlanta candidates sit ASNT's exams. This section covers where they train, and how to pick.

Who offers NDT training around Atlanta?

  • Applied Technical Services (ATS), Marietta. Beyond its exam work, ATS runs NDT courses at its Marietta location and in Greenville, South Carolina, which it says run on a weekly basis. The catalogue covers eddy current, visual, penetrant, magnetic particle, radiography and ultrasonic testing, mostly at Level I and II, plus a Level III refresher, film interpretation, radiation safety, UT thickness and aircraft wheel inspection. Each course mixes theory with hands-on work and ends with a written completion exam, and ATS also offers training at the customer's site.
  • Chattanooga State Community College. About two hours north, the college offers NDT as a concentration of its Engineering Technology associate degree, which ABET accredits. Six methods are taught; embedded certificates mark progress through the surface methods, the volumetric methods and weld and visual inspection, and each one needs written and practical exams that a Level III gives or approves. TVA staff helped develop the programme when it launched.
  • Welding schools. Tulsa Welding School lists a metro Atlanta location in Decatur. Welding programmes teach visual weld inspection; ask whether a given programme includes any method-level NDT.
  • Employer training. Field service companies hire trainees and advance them under their own written practices.

What Atlanta employers ask for

Field roles out of Atlanta can call for advanced UT. A MISTRAS posting for PAUT technicians in Atlanta required a current PAUT Level II or Level III, a prior Level II in shear-wave UT with a year of experience or an SNT-TC-1A Level II in phased array, and previous PAUT field work. It preferred corrosion mapping, encoded weld scans and extra certifications such as MT, PT, VT or TOFD, and expected a valid driver's licence, extensive US travel and outage and shutdown schedules. Read that as a ladder: shear-wave UT Level II first, then phased array, then the field hours.

Engine and airframe work at the airport follows a different path, set by the maintenance organisation's own written practice. If that is your target, read aviation NDT training before choosing a course.

How to choose an Atlanta NDT course

  • Short course or degree? A week-long method course suits someone already employed in NDT. A degree suits a school leaver who wants broad method coverage and lab time before a first job.
  • Completion exam versus certification. Passing a course's completion exam is a training record. Certification comes later, from the employer, once its Level III has examined you.
  • Hours against SNT-TC-1A. Confirm the course hours meet the recommendation for your method and level; the hours planner shows the targets.
  • Path to PAUT. If phased array is the goal, check that the provider expects shear-wave UT first, as employers do.
  • Time off work. Weekly in-person courses mean days away from a shift; self-paced theory does not.

Where the Atlantis route fits for Atlanta technicians

You will not find an Atlantis classroom in Atlanta. Theory for each method sits in an online course you work through on your own timetable, questions go to an ASNT NDT Level III, and the course opens the day you sign up, in any month. Practice in the Practical NDT simulator comes before the real thing. The supervised hands-on practical and the practical exam are done at your employer's site on equipment it owns, following its SNT-TC-1A-based written practice, and the employer is the one that certifies.

For the PAUT ladder above, the sequence is ultrasonic testing training to Level II, then phased array training, with the phased array simulator for set-up practice. Atlanta inspection companies hiring trainees can have an Atlantis Level III set up the written practice and examinations through SNT-TC-1A training programme set-up. Elsewhere in Georgia or across the line? See NDT training in Georgia or NDT training in Chattanooga.
